newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares drop 1.7 pct ahead of long weekend.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares drop 1.7 pct ahead of long weekend.

text.p: Delhi shares closer sharply lower on Thursday as speculators and domestic institutions unloaded stocks on the last day of the fortnightly settlement period and before a long weekend, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's benchmark index fell 15.64 points, or 1.7 percent, to close at 907.26.
The bourse will be shut for four days and trading will resume next Tuesday. Friday is a holiday on account of India's Independence Day, and the Hindu festival of Raksha Bandhan falls on Monday.
Traders said players were reluctant to stake out new positions and were expected to resume buying activity in the next settlement period starting on Tuesday.

"In the absence of any encouraging factor, the speculative activity also dropped considerably forcing operators to adopt a wait-and-watch strategy," Manoj Aggarwal of stock broking firm Multiple Investments said.
"Stocks of automobile and multinational companies were losers during the session on large-scale selling by speculators," another broker said.
Nestle India fell nine rupees to end at 280. The firm announced that net profit from operations was unchanged in the six months to June 29, at 223 million rupees.
Reliance Industries first surged to 374.25 rupees, then fell to 369, before closing 0.70 rupee lower at 371.25.
TISCO see-sawed in the range of 207.25 to 203 rupees before recovering partially to end 1.70 rupees lower at 204.50.
State Bank of India gained 1.25 rupees to close at 323.95.
The shares of multinational companies fell on late selling, brokers said.
ITC dipped 3.50 rupees to end at 569 after rising to 578 earlier.
Bajaj Auto lost eight rupees to finish at 869.
TELCO dropped 1.05 rupees to close at 371.
Telephone company MTNL faced sizeable selling pressure and slid 7.90 rupees to end at 275 rupees.
ACC Ltd lost 10 rupees to close at 1,560.
